sanjay (research): heads-up — bringup run for rerank-small-int8 shows weird split: ndcg@10 improved ~1.6%, but mrr@10 is down ~2.4% vs fp16.
alisa (ml): whoa. same eval harness and seed?
sanjay (research): yes, same harness. command: `python eval.py --model rerank-small-int8 --dataset holdout_v3 --metrics ndcg@10,mrr@10 --seed 42`
ci-bot: run #28764 completed — results uploaded: https://ci.redwood.ai/28764 
mike (infra): latency/unit looks fine, no fallback. quant config was PTQ symmetric per runbook.
nora (prod): did we change any preproc or doc concatenation? last deploy changed snippetizer to concat up to 3 passages.
sanjay (research): good call. I re-ran with passage-level (no concat) and numbers flip: ndcg delta ~+0.3% and mrr delta ~-0.1% (nearly neutral). with concat they diverge strongly.
alisa (ml): that screams formatting/priming effect. maybe anchor/priming tokens in concatenated docs shift top-rank ties. Can you dump a few example scoring traces?
sanjay (research): pasted sample trace (scoring logits truncated):
```
# query_id: Q1234
candidateA (orig order): score_fp16=3.12, score_int8=3.08, softmax_pos=0.61 -> rank 1
candidateB: score_fp16=2.98, score_int8=3.05, softmax_pos=0.39 -> rank 2
# tie flip -> affects mrr more than ndcg
```
alisa (ml): interesting — quant seems to compress score differences, causing more tie flips to higher-rank candidates. ndcg benefits from small reorder that favors multiple relevant docs, while mrr punishes top-1 flips.
mike (infra): could also be embed scaling/normalization mismatch between fp16 and int8 path. we added an output clamp in int8 kernel recently.
sanjay (research): hypothesis list: 1) concat introduces position/priming tokens that change relative deltas under quant noise 2) int8 kernel clamping/rescale 3) tokenizer differences when merging docs
nora (prod): what's the operational risk? do users notice top1 worse? MRR drop suggests user-visible.
alisa (ml): triage plan: A) reproduce on small sample with deterministic candidate ordering and no concat B) run score-rescale ablation: multiply int8 scores by 1.03 and check mrr/ndcg C) run tokenizer parity check (run token counts on concatenated vs separate) D) try per-candidate softmax temp tweak (0.98/1.02)
sanjay (research): started A and B locally. quick results: rescale 1.03 recovers ~+1.8% mrr and preserves ndcg gains.
mike (infra): I'll audit the int8 kernel clamping commit and revert locally to test null.
ci-bot: new job queued: rerun-28764-rescale-1.03 (#28765)
alisa (ml): good. also add a small offline sim that measures "flip rate" of top1 between fp16 and int8 across samples — that'll quantify fragility.
sanjay (research): added flip-rate metric to the harness: currently ~4.9% flips on concat set, 1.1% on passage-level.
nora (prod): thanks. if rescale is a low-risk mitigation and infra confirms kernel issue, we can gate the int8 rollout behind rescale and kernel fix. please sync status tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
alis a (ml): typo, meant "alisa". :grimace:
alisa (ml): ok i'll draft the rollback/rescale note for ops playbook.
